chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who borrows white dirhams by number, then pays back black (darker/heavier) dirhams by weight, knowing that they are heavier than what he took, and he is pleased to keep the excess for himself. He said: 'There is no harm, provided he had not stipulated it; if he had gifted them all to him, it would have been valid for him.'

key_terms.اَلسُّودَ: Black dirhams (heavier or lower purity coins)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to repay a loan with heavier coins and keep the difference?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *fadl* (excess) in debt repayment when the returned currency differs in weight or quality, provided the lender voluntarily accepts it as a gift rather than it being a pre-stipulated condition. It highlights the Shia juristic distinction between a contractual obligation and a gratuitous transfer, ensuring that the transaction remains free from *riba* (usury) as long as the excess is not guaranteed by the contract terms. This ruling is foundational in understanding how early Islamic scholars navigated the complexities of debased coinage and varying metal standards in commercial transactions.
